answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through synchronous pseudonym parties. At a global admission inlet, human sponsors join randomly shuffled live video rooms simultaneously to cross-sign one blinded credential per attendee, tying an agent to a verified identity thread. Because one person cannot credibly attend multiple rooms at once, each fake identity costs simultaneous human presence. Yet real-time deepfakes staged in dim umber lighting can still deceive peer reviewers and leak duplicate seats.
